title: Industry Pulse — AI / Agent Ecosystem

bullets.title: OpenAI ships GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna at roughly half the price of GPT-5.6
bullets.summary: Released 22 Sep: Sol at $2/$10 and Luna at $0.10/$0.50 per Mtok as permanent pricing, with OpenAI claiming Sol makes about half as many factual mistakes as its predecessor; live in API, Codex and ChatGPT.
bullets.how: Luna is a cheap candidate for high-volume Construct batch work (alt text, classification); for PRAGMA, a new model tier to re-measure client visibility against.

bullets.title: Baselayer raises $35M Series A (M13) and launches 'Know Your Agent' identity for AI agents
bullets.summary: Announced 22 Sep: the bank identity-verification vendor's Agentic Identity Suite checks who deployed an agent, who it represents and whether it may transact.
bullets.how: Signals that agent identity/authorization is becoming buyer-facing infrastructure; a PRAGMA talking point for clients letting agents act on their behalf. No direct B9 use.

bullets.title: arXiv 2609.15906: Authorization Architectures for Tool-Using AI Agents
bullets.summary: September paper laying out a principal hierarchy (user, operator, orchestrator, sub-agent, tool endpoint) and five layers: identity/credentials, delegation and scope propagation, runtime enforcement, prompt injection as authorization bypass, and auditability.
bullets.how: A ready checklist for The Construct's credential-bearing skills and Hermes loops: scope what each sub-agent inherits and log it.

bullets.title: Ema raises $77M Series B for 'AI employees' in enterprise HR, IT and finance
bullets.summary: Announced 23 Sep (Creagis lead, Accel returning): Ema's prebuilt agents plan and execute tasks inside existing enterprise systems and escalate sensitive actions to a human approver; it cites Wipro and Hitachi deployments.
bullets.how: Validates PRAGMA's packaged-operator pitch (prebuilt role agents, not DIY frameworks) and the approve-before-sensitive-action pattern The Construct already uses; no direct B9 use.

bullets.title: Rabbit launches OS3, a cloud personal agent that drives your own computers, imports skills from other agents, and pairs to your phone over Telegram
bullets.summary: Unveiled 23 Sep: bring-your-own-key and model-agnostic (Claude, GPT, OpenRouter or local), installs on up to five machines with one command, swaps models without losing memory or skills, and requires confirmation for sensitive actions; SiliconANGLE lists Hermes Agent as a direct comparable.
bullets.how: Same shape as The Construct (Hermes on the Mac, Telegram to Bobby, skills as portable assets); if import-a-skill-by-URL becomes a cross-agent standard, Construct skills become sellable PRAGMA deliverables. No B9 use.

praxis_lesson: Three of today's five items are about agents acting with borrowed authority, and a fourth (Rabbit OS3) is a consumer product built the same way The Construct is: model-agnostic, skills as portable assets, consent on sensitive actions. As models get cheaper and swappable, the durable assets are the skills and the permission scoping around them, not the model underneath.
